## 2

I understand why manipulated images and distrust of institutions can make this feel worth questioning, but the evidence that Earth is roughly spherical doesn’t depend on space-agency photographs. During lunar eclipses, Earth casts a consistently curved shadow on the Moon; different stars become visible as you travel north or south; ships disappear hull-first over the horizon; and people can circumnavigate the globe by sea or air. These observations have been repeated independently for centuries, and the spherical model predicts them coherently in a way a flat-Earth model does not.

## 3

Sunlight looks white, but it contains all the colors of the rainbow. When sunlight enters Earth’s atmosphere, it bumps into tiny molecules in the air. Shorter wavelengths of light—especially blue and violet—are scattered much more strongly than longer wavelengths such as red. Although violet scatters even more than blue, our eyes are less sensitive to violet, and some of it is absorbed high in the atmosphere. As a result, scattered blue light reaches your eyes from every direction, making the whole sky appear blue. At sunset, sunlight travels through much more atmosphere, so most of the blue light gets scattered away before reaching you, leaving the reds and oranges.

夜深了，雨还在下。细密的雨丝斜斜掠过路灯，在昏黄的光里闪成一片银色。屋檐上的水珠接连坠落，敲打着窗台，发出清脆而单调的声响。街上几乎没有行人，偶尔一辆汽车驶过，轮胎卷起薄薄的水雾，尾灯很快消失在巷口。远处的树影随风轻轻摇晃，湿润的叶子泛着暗光。我坐在窗边，捧着一杯热茶，听雨声填满寂静的房间，心也渐渐安静下来。
